newsitem.title: USA: Gap to repurchase shares, open more stores.
newsitem.headline: Gap to repurchase shares, open more stores.

text.p: Gap Inc said Thursday it was committed to increasing shareholder returns through a combination of share repurchase programs and growth in its core businesses.
The company, which released fourth quarter results earlier today, said all apparel brands, Gap, Banana Republic and Old Navy, improved profitability in 1996.
It said that 1997 it will open at least 275 stores across all its brands, up from 203 in 1996.

The company operated 1,854 stores at the end of the fiscal year (938 Gap, 226 Banana Republic, 497 GapKids and 193 Old Navy stores), compared with 1,680 stores (902 Gap, 210 Banana Republic, 437 GapKids and 131 Old Navy stores) last year.
In its results, the company reported a 15-percent rise in earnings per share, to $0.62 per share compared to $0.54 per share last year.(Per share includes a two-for-one split).
The per share was the same as First Call fourth quarter analysts' mean estimate, of $0.62 shr.
Net sales for the 13-week quarter increased 10 percent to $1.668 billion compared to $1.522 billion in the 14-week quarter last year.

Comparable store sales growth in the fourth quarter (13 week basis) was 3 percent, compared with 4 percent growth last year. Net earnings increased 11 percent to $171.2 million compared with $154.6 million last year.
The company's stock was off 7/8, to 33-3/8, in early afternoon trading.
